windows.label: Human
windows.text: Often times the breakup is hard, but the aftermath is worse. Public demonization should be avoided, but I don’t think that means hiding the truth about the relationship to save face. Sometimes the truth is that you were abused, coerced, or seriously deceived.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
So how much you say, and to whom, and how publicly, really depends on what happened and why you’re telling people.
Once you’re out, you can see things you genuinely couldn’t see while you were bonded. Look at what you contributed.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Try to understand whatever was true in your ex’s perspective too, including the conflicts they were carrying inside themselves, and don’t turn them into a cartoon villain.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Sometimes the easiest story is that they were fake all along, because it explains everything. Grab it only if it really is the simplest explanation of what happened.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: People who aren’t heavily invested in seeing your innocence can help you tell, and a therapist, pastor, or even a stranger may see the evidence more clearly than a lifelong friend.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Even the curiosity itself can be therapeutic for you.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Spiritual practice during an ending is critical, but don’t use it to get around the feelings.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Pray for your ex’s wellbeing.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Remember what was real and good, and don’t use your pain as permission to hate them. Avoid the New Age belief that everyone is simply a mirror of you.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: No, that isn’t true. We partly mirror one another, but each person was formed by plenty that had nothing to do with you.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: No matter how enlightened the Buddha was, his cousin Devadatta still kept trying to kill him.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Looking honestly at your part doesn’t erase theirs.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Sometimes it helps to ask, “What would Mr.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
Rogers do?” (if you’re old enough to remember that show).
I also learned that public demonization doesn’t always have to be the last chapter. If you avoid contact forever, they might never apologize and learn honesty. But it can help to keep distance for a while until cooler heads prevail. It can be tempting to let them back into your life after a private apology, and especially after a public one, but keep in mind you deserve a stable love.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: You’re not a yo-yo.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Once I’m attached, “I’m taking a chance on her” starts turning into “she’s the right person” after we’ve been together for a while.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Based on what? Sometimes I actually learned something, and sometimes nothing changed except that now I’m attached, so the new certainty is just harder for me to question.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: If I have sex with somebody quickly, that’s a reason not to move in quickly too.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Moving in together right away is basically getting into a common-law marriage without discussing it, and it’s too easy for me to assume the relationship is going well just because we’re already entangled.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: So I want us to keep seeing friends and have some kind of community around the relationship, and I want us to pick actual dates to ask how it’s going.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
I can know I want her much faster than I can know whether I want to raise children with her, live in community with her, or build a life with her.
At some point one of you will ask, “Why am I special to you? Why are you with me and not somebody else?” If the answer is basically, “We had sex and got hitched?” I don’t know, that’s a damn shame.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: And then there’s the situationship, which is hard to define because that’s basically the point. Usually it’s a happenstance relationship based on sex. There’s less communication, and what communication exists is more superficial. Yet it is obviously some kind of relationship even while one or both people refuse to name it. You’re regularly having sex, going out together, spending time alone together, and doing things you wouldn’t do with a regular friend, so it feels like it’s filling a relationship void, but only accidentally and occasionally—maybe just enough to keep you from looking for anything deeper.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: It can go either way. Often the man wants to keep it undefined while the woman wants commitment, partly because she’s the one risking pregnancy.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: If you’re the one keeping it undefined, you get the fun without the responsibility.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Refusing to name the relationship doesn’t make the responsibility disappear, though, and you don’t escape the existential void created by another superficial fix.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Doomscrolling entertains you too.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: People call oxytocin the “love hormone,” as if getting more attached should make you feel closer and safer. If closeness was safe when you were little, maybe it does feel a bit like coming home, but if it came with neglect, abuse, or if people disappeared on you, you can get more attached and more freaked out at the same time. You might get anxious or suspicious. You might feel worthless or fight or flight mode may kick in.

r12-peek.headline: Human Written

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Before the wisdom window closes, the main thing is to find out whether you are actually compatible. Do you have the same goals and values, especially around children, religion, politics, health, love, and romance? Where do you want to live? Do you both want to find a community? What kind of relationship do you want with technology and money?

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Ask deep questions.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
Conversation-card games may seem silly, but they can help people get past superficial talk and see if they’re compatible.
But asking, “How do you handle jealousy?” can get me a beautiful answer that tells me almost nothing. I’d rather ask what she thinks she would do in an actual situation. If all she can give me is a general answer, I assume she probably doesn’t know yet.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: A card game can create its own little high too.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
If we spend two hours telling each other things nobody else knows, we may feel incredibly understood and close, but that may mean the game worked without telling us whether the relationship will.
You can also bring the person to a party and see how they act, bring them around your family or friends, or take them to activities you enjoy and see if they really enjoy them too. Try doing what you would normally do in your day alone, but with them, and see how it feels.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Is it weird?

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Are they wondering why you do this stuff? Do they look bored, like they’d rather just hit you up later than be with you while you’re doing ordinary stuff? Can you guys be normal together and not just romantic or dating?

windows.label: Human
windows.text: See their negative side first too.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
If there is no negative side, that’s a red flag for fakery. Ask whether the spiritual story they tell about themselves survives an inconvenient PMS afternoon. How recent is the healing story—two months or two years? Jealousy, abandonment, possessiveness, and the “I’m so much better than I used to be” story may not be understood until there is stress and entanglement. By then, of course, you’re stressed and entangled. 😆
Sometimes the only thing I have is a little “wait” feeling.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: It doesn’t prove anything.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
But if I’m about to ignore a question because I really want this to work, that’s enough reason for me to ask the question before I keep going.
If they’re nasty to their friends, family, or other people, assume they will eventually be nasty to you. We mostly seem to get attracted to the inner-child part because we’re coming from our inner child and we want to have fun. But you also need to find out whether there is a healthy adult there before you’re too bonded to want the answer.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
Couples withdraw from friends who aren’t supportive of the romantic dyad, and they also stop telling friends the whole truth. Sharp questions start to feel rude. An obvious problem dissolves into, “but I love her,” and the small world of the relationship starts feeling more real than the rest of life, right when both people most need a view from outside it.
Sometimes withdrawing isn’t wrong: telling your friend, “Can you believe what my girlfriend is doing to me?” can be a privacy violation. It’s just important to realize what is happening.
It doesn’t help if she tells her friends her side while I tell mine mine, so we need people who actually know both of us over time, well enough that the relationship isn’t the only reality in the room. I’ll come back to that.
